items.title: Escape lemma for manifold flows: a finite maximal time forces the integral curve to leave every compact set
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $M$ be a smooth
manifold without boundary, let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), let $p\in M$ and
let $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ be the unique maximal integral curve of $X$
with $\gamma(0)=p$ ([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]],
[[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]). If $\beta<+\infty$ then for every
compact set $K\subseteq M$
([[def-compact-space]]) there is $s\in(\alpha,\beta)$ such that
$\gamma(t)\notin K$ for every $t\in(s,\beta)$. Dually, if $\alpha>-\infty$
then for every compact $K$ there is $s$ such that $\gamma(t)\notin K$ for
every $t\in(\alpha,s)$.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed., Springer GTM 218 (2012): the escape lemma for integral curves (Lemma 9.19 in the second edition), with the maximal integral curve and local flow theorem
Gerald Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems: maximal solutions and escape from compact sets, Chapter 2

items.title: A pointwise convergent subsequence of a uniformly Lipschitz family into a compact metric space converges uniformly on compact subintervals
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(B,d)$ be a compact metric space
([[def-metric-space]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior, let $K\ge0$ be real, and let $\sigma_m:I\to B$,
$m\in\mathbb N$, be $K$-Lipschitz maps,
$d(\sigma_m(s),\sigma_m(t))\le K|s-t|$ for all $s,t\in I$. Then there are a
strictly increasing sequence $m_1<m_2<\cdots$ and a $K$-Lipschitz map
$\sigma:I\to B$ such that $\sigma_{m_j}\to\sigma$ uniformly on every compact
subinterval of $I$.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems: the diagonal subsequence argument and Arzela-Ascoli type compactness on compact metric targets, Chapter 2
Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis I: dense subsets of the line and uniform convergence on compact intervals, Sections 6.3 and 7.4

items.title: Existence of a positive smooth volume density of total mass one on a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a nonempty time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with the
metric volume coefficient $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a) in charts. Then
there is a positive smooth density $r$ on $M$ in the following sense: in the
coefficient formulation of
[[def-borel-measurable-nonnegative-density-on-a-manifold]], $r$ is the
nonnegative density whose chart coefficients are smooth functions, and
$r>0$ at every point. Its glued density measure
$\mu:=\mu_r$ of [[def-countable-chart-gluing-of-a-nonnegative-density-measure]]
and [[thm-chart-gluing-defines-a-countably-additive-borel-density-measure]]
satisfies:

**(a)** $\mu(M)=1$, and $\mu$ is a compact-finite, locally finite,
$\sigma$-finite regular Borel measure;

**(b)** $\mu(O)>0$ for every nonempty open $O\subseteq M$;

**(c)** local absolute continuity. For every chart $(V,y)$ of $M$ and every
Borel set $E\subseteq V$ whose image $y(E)$ is Lebesgue null in
$\mathbb R^4$, one has $\mu(E)=0$.

references.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): the volume function construction (partition of unity, finite positive smooth density and normalization), proof of Theorem 2.11.1, printed pp. 57-58

S. W. Hawking and G. F. R. Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time, Cambridge University Press (1973): the volume measure in the proof that a Cauchy surface implies global hyperbolicity, section 6.6

items.title: Causal cone domination in adapted charts and Lipschitz-graph bounds for causal curves
items.statement:
For the absolutely continuous curve conclusion (c), assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) as required by the cited causal-curve calculus and fundamental theorem. The other clauses use the given smooth observer structure, pointwise adapted-chart existence and finite compactness arguments, without these additional curve-calculus premises. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), and put $n=N/\sqrt{-g(N,N)}$. Write $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. In a chart $(U,x)$ put $v^a=dx^a(v)$, $v_s=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and $|v|_{\mathrm e}=(\sum_{a=0}^3(v^a)^2)^{1/2}$.

**(a) Adapted orthonormal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there are a chart $(U,x)$, $x(p)=0$, a radius $r>0$ with $U=x^{-1}(B_r)$, and $K\ge1$, such that on all of $U$
$$n=\partial_{x^0},\qquad g_{00}\equiv-1,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}.$$

**(b) Cone domination.** The chart and radius in (a) can be chosen so every nonzero future causal vector at any point of $U$ satisfies
$$|v_s|\le K v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le K v^0\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad v^0\ge K^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$

**(c) Curve form.** Every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] has strictly increasing time coordinate, and for all $s<t$ in $I$
$$x^0(\gamma(s))<x^0(\gamma(t)),\qquad |x_s(\gamma(t))-x_s(\gamma(s))|\le K\left(x^0(\gamma(t))-x^0(\gamma(s))\right).$$
Consequently every spatial component satisfies the same bound, and the curve image is the graph of a $K$-Lipschitz function into Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ over the interval $x^0(\gamma(I))$.

**(d) Flat minorant cone.** The same chart can be chosen so the constant-coordinate metric $\eta_{16}=-(dx^0)^2+16\sum_i(dx^i)^2$ has every nonzero $\eta_{16}$-causal vector $g$-timelike throughout $U$. If $q,q'\in U$ and $\eta_{16}(x(q')-x(q),x(q')-x(q))<0$, then $q\ll q'$ if $x^0(q')>x^0(q)$, and $q'\ll q$ otherwise.

**(e) General temporal charts: exact compact uniformity.** For any chart $(U',z)$ define its temporal locus
$$P=\{q\in U':\nabla z^0(q)\text{ is past timelike}\}.$$
For every compact set $K_0\subset P$ there is $L\ge1$ such that all nonzero future causal vectors based in $K_0$, with coordinate components and Euclidean norm taken in $z$, satisfy
$$|v_s|\le L v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le L v^0,\qquad v^0\ge L^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$
In particular these bounds hold throughout any relatively compact $U_0\Subset U'$ whose closure is contained in $P$, equivalently whose time gradient is past timelike on its entire closure. Timelikeness merely on $U_0$ gives local bounds at each point and uniform bounds on each compact subset of $U_0$; it does not alone give a uniform bound on all of $U_0$.

No additional choice is used to select the pointwise linear bases or compact cone constants. Countable and Dependent Choice are explicitly required only for the general absolutely continuous curve clause (c), through its actual calculus suppliers.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: the local time coordinate and Lipschitz parametrization of causal curves (Lemma 1.33, Theorem 2.12 and Remark 2.13 printed pp. 29-33; Theorem 2.87 proof printed pp. 60-61)
S. W. Hawking and G. F. R. Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time, Cambridge University Press (1973): the local Lipschitz behaviour of causal curves, section 6.2

items.title: The auxiliary Riemannian metric h=g+2n-flat tensor n-flat is complete after a proper-exhaustion conformal factor, and its closed bounded sets are compact
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}}\quad\text{(pointwise)},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat,$$
with the flat map $\flat$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
so that $h$ is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then:

**(a)** $h$ is a smooth Riemannian (positive definite) metric on $M$.

**(b)** There is a smooth nonnegative proper function $f:M\to[0,\infty)$ such
that the metric
$$h':=(1+|df|_h^2)\,h$$
is a smooth Riemannian metric with $|df|_{h'}\le1$ everywhere.

**(c)** For each connected component $M_0$ of $M$, the metric space
$(M_0,d_{h'})$ is complete, where $d_{h'}$ is the Riemannian distance of
$h'|_{M_0}$ ([[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]],
[[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]]).

**(d)** Consequently, for every connected component $M_0$, every subset of
$M_0$ that is closed in $M_0$ and bounded in $d_{h'}$ is compact, and every
closed ball $\{q\in M_0:d_{h'}(q,p)\le r\}$ is compact.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: auxiliary Riemannian metrics, section 1.6 with Theorem 1.5 (Nomizu-Ozeki; a complete metric in every conformal class) and the Hopf-Rinow compactness of closed balls, printed pp. 10-11; Definition 2.16 and Lemma 2.17 (h-arclength of inextendible causal curves), printed pp. 33-34
R. M. Wald, General Relativity, University of Chicago Press (1984): the auxiliary positive definite metric on a time-oriented spacetime, Chapter 8

items.title: Future sets, past sets, achronal boundaries and their elementary properties
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
chronological and causal relations $\ll$, $\le$ and the sets $I^\pm$,
$J^\pm$ of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Future and past sets.** A subset $F\subseteq M$ is a **future set**
when $I^+(F)\subseteq F$, where $I^+(F)=\bigcup_{p\in F}I^+(p)$; it is a
**past set** when $I^-(F)\subseteq F$. A future set is **open** when it is
open in the manifold topology; for an open future set one has
$F=I^+(F)$.

**(b) Achronal boundary.** A set $A\subseteq M$ is an **achronal boundary**
when $A=\partial F$ for a future set $F$; by (c) below this is equivalent to
$A=\partial F$ for an open future set.

**(c) Elementary properties.** The following are immediate from the
openness of $I^\pm$ and the transitivity of $\ll$
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (f)):

- if $F$ is a future set then its complement is a past set, and conversely;
- $I^\pm(S)$, $J^\pm(S)$ and $\overline{J^\pm(S)}$ are future (respectively
  past) sets for every $S\subseteq M$;
- if $F$ is a future set then $F$ is open if and only if $I^+(F)=F$, and
  then $\partial F$ is achronal: if $p,q\in\partial F$ with $p\ll q$, then
  $q\in I^+(p)\subseteq I^+(F)\subseteq F$, so $q$ is interior to $F$
  (because $I^+(p)$ is open in $F$ through $q$), contradicting
  $q\in\partial F$;
- a set $S$ is achronal in the sense of
  [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (b) if and only
  if $\overline S$ is achronal, because $I^\pm$ is open in its arguments.

**(d) Scope.** These are set-theoretic definitions inside the smooth
Lorentzian model; they assert nothing about existence of achronal
boundaries with additional regularity, and they carry no physical
interpretation here.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: future and past sets (Definition 2.83 printed p. 59), achronal boundaries (Definition 2.86 printed p. 60) and their elementary properties (Proposition 2.84 printed pp. 59-60)
S. W. Hawking and G. F. R. Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time, Cambridge University Press (1973): future and past sets and achronal boundaries, section 6.3

items.title: Strong causality bounds the auxiliary length of causal curves contained in a compact set
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous curve calculus and its fundamental theorem. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a strongly causal time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(b)) and let $h$ be a smooth positive definite metric on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then for every compact set
$K\subseteq M$ there is $L(K)\in[0,\infty)$ such that
$$\ell_h(\gamma)\le L(K)$$
for every future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with $\gamma([a,b])\subseteq K$.

Consequently, if $\gamma$ is parametrized by $h$-arclength
($\ell_h(\gamma|_{[s,t]})=t-s$) and its image is contained in the compact set
$K$, then $b-a\le L(K)$.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Theorem 2.80 (a strongly causal spacetime is non-partially imprisoning) with proof, printed p. 58, and Theorem 1.35/Definition 1.34 on strong causality, printed p. 24

S. W. Hawking and G. F. R. Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time, Cambridge University Press (1973): strong causality and the finite number of causally convex neighbourhoods met by a causal curve, section 6.2

items.title: Failure of strong causality yields causal curves escaping one fixed neighbourhood with endpoints accumulating at the point
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Countable Choice selects the sequence of escape witnesses; the stated AC curve-calculus suppliers require both premises. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $p\in M$. Suppose that strong
causality fails at $p$ ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]
clause (b)): there is an open neighborhood $U$ of $p$ such that for every
open $V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ there are a future causal curve
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) $\sigma$ and parameters $s<t$ in
its domain with
$$\sigma(s),\sigma(t)\in V,\qquad \sigma([s,t])\not\subseteq V .$$
Then there exist an open set $W$ with $p\in W$ and $\overline W\subseteq U$
and, for every $k\ge2$, points $x_k,y_k\in W$ with $x_k\to p$ and
$y_k\to p$, together with future causal curves $\sigma_k:[0,1]\to M$ with
$\sigma_k(0)=x_k$, $\sigma_k(1)=y_k$ and
$$\sigma_k([0,1])\not\subseteq W .$$
No additional choice is used beyond these stated premises.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Theorem 1.35 (the local basis of causally convex sets with V_{k+1} causally convex in V_k, equations (1.6)-(1.7) and proof, printed pp. 24-25); Theorem 2.69 (failure of strong causality yields an inextendible continuous causal curve through the point) with proof, printed pp. 54-55

P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): proof of Theorem 2.9.9 (the sequence of causal curves exiting and re-entering the h-balls, printed pp. 48-50) and Definition 2.2.7 with Proposition 2.2.3 (elementary regions) printed pp. 8-13

items.title: The joint exponential map: smoothness, invertible differential at the diagonal, and the small-velocity two-point inverse
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
geodesics, their maximal domains $I_{q,v}$ and the exponential maps
$\exp_q$ be those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Fix
$p\in M$. Write $\pi:TM\to M$ for the bundle projection.

**(a) Smoothness of the joint map.** The set
$$\mathcal D:=\{(q,v)\in TM:\ 1\in I_{q,v}\}\subseteq TM$$
is open in $TM$, and the **joint exponential map**
$$\Phi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M\times M,\qquad \Phi(q,v):=(q,\exp_q v),$$
is smooth.

**(b) Differential at $(p,0)$.** The differential $d\Phi_{(p,0)}$ is an
isomorphism. Explicitly, fix a smooth chart $(U,x)$ around $p$; it induces
the chart $(TU,Tx)$ of $TM$ and the product chart $(U\times U,x\times x)$ of
$M\times M$, and under the induced identifications
$T_{(p,0)}(TM)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ and
$T_{(p,p)}(M\times M)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ one has
$$d\Phi_{(p,0)}(u,w)=(u,\ u+w)\qquad\text{for all }u,w\in T_pM .$$

**(c) Diffeomorphism and two-point inverse.** There are open neighborhoods
$V\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $(p,0)$ and $W\subseteq M\times M$ of $(p,p)$ such
that $\Phi|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Moreover $V$ can be chosen
product-like: there are a chart $(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$, a radius
$r>0$ and a velocity radius $\rho>0$ such that, writing $B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb
R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$,
$$V=\bigl\{(q,v):\ q\in x^{-1}(B_r),\ \text{the coordinate components of }v\text{ in }(TU,Tx)\text{ lie in }B_\rho\bigr\},$$
and there is $s\in(0,r)$ with $x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$.
Consequently the velocity map
$$v:W\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (q,r)\longmapsto v(q,r):=\text{the vector with }(q,v(q,r))\in V,\ \Phi(q,v(q,r))=(q,r),$$
is well defined and smooth, and $\exp_q\bigl(v(q,r)\bigr)=r$ for all
$(q,r)\in W$.

**(d) Lipschitz bound for the two-point inverse.** On every pair
$x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$ as in (c) there is a constant
$\Lambda\ge 0$ such that, for all $q,r\in x^{-1}(B_s)$,
$$|v(q,r)|_x\le\Lambda\,\bigl|x(q)-x(r)\bigr|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $|v|_x$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate components of
$v$ and $v(q,q)=0$. In particular $|v(q,r)|_x\le 2\Lambda s$ on this pair.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: normal neighborhoods (Definition 2.2 printed p. 26) and Theorem 2.4 with the joint exponential diffeomorphism onto pairs of nearby points (printed p. 26); Gauss' Lemma and the position vector (Definition 2.5, Theorem 2.6 printed pp. 26-27)
P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): the exponential map and normal neighborhoods, sections 2.2-2.4

items.title: Convexity of the Euclidean radius function along geodesics: segments with endpoints in a small ball stay in the ball
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and let geodesics be those of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth
chart of $M$ and write $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with its Euclidean norm
$|\cdot|_{\mathrm e}$ on $x(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^4$; write
$B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$ and, for a compact subset
$K\subseteq U$, let
$$\|\Gamma\|_K:=\sup_{y\in x(K)}\ \sup_{|u|_{\mathrm e}=|v|_{\mathrm e}=1}|\Gamma(y)[u,v]|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $\Gamma(y)[u,v]^a=\sum_{b,c=0}^3\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(y)u^bv^c$. Thus this is the Euclidean bilinear operator norm, not the maximum of the individual coefficients; set $\|\Gamma\|_{\varnothing}=0$. The Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]].

**(a) Second-derivative inequality.** Let $\gamma:J\to U$ be a geodesic and
let $f:J\to\mathbb R$, $f(t):=|x(\gamma(t))|_{\mathrm e}^2$, where the norm is
the Euclidean norm of the chart image. At every parameter $t\in J$,
$$f''(t)=2\bigl|\dot x(t)\bigr|_{\mathrm e}^2-2\,x(t)\cdot\Gamma(x(t))[\dot x(t),\dot x(t)],$$
where $\Gamma(x)[\dot x,\dot x]$ is the vector with components
$\sum_{i,j}\Gamma^a{}_{ij}(x)\dot x^i\dot x^j$ and $\cdot$ is the Euclidean
scalar product. Consequently, along every geodesic whose image lies in a
fixed compact $K\subseteq U$,
$$f''\ge 2\bigl(1-\|\Gamma\|_K\,|x(\gamma)|\bigr)\bigl|\dot x\bigr|_{\mathrm e}^2 .$$
In particular, if $x(K)\subseteq B_{r_1}$ and $\|\Gamma\|_K\,r_1\le\tfrac12$
then $f''\ge|\dot x|_{\mathrm e}^2\ge0$ at every parameter of such a
geodesic.

**(b) Maximum principle.** Let $\gamma:[0,1]\to U$ be a geodesic whose image
is contained in a compact $K$ with $x(K)\subseteq B_{r_1}$ and
$\|\Gamma\|_K\,r_1\le\frac12$, and suppose
$|x(\gamma(0))|_{\mathrm e}\le r_2$ and $|x(\gamma(1))|_{\mathrm e}\le r_2$
for some $r_2<r_1$. Then
$$|x(\gamma(t))|_{\mathrm e}\le r_2\qquad\text{for every }t\in[0,1].$$

references.title: E. Minguzzi and M. Sanchez, On the existence of maximal curves and the Heine-Borel property of a spacetime, arXiv:2012.15460 (2020 revision), and E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: convexity of small balls, section 2.2 printed pp. 26-27

P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Proposition 2.2.6 with proof (printed pp. 12-13), geodesic convexity of small coordinate balls and the second-derivative estimate along geodesics

items.title: Speed bounds along geodesics in a chart, and small initial velocity of every geodesic segment contained in a small ball
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $(U,x)$ be a chart,
$B_s=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$ and let $K\subseteq U$ be compact
with $\|\Gamma\|_K<\infty$ as in
[[lem-gr-coordinate-ball-geodesic-convexity]]. Let $\gamma:[0,1]\to U$ be a
geodesic, write $s\mapsto w(s):=|\dot x(s)|_{\mathrm e}$ for the Euclidean
norm of its coordinate velocity, and let
$$v_0:=w(0).$$

**(a) Two-sided speed bounds.** If $0\le\delta\le1$, $4\|\Gamma\|_K v_0\delta\le1$, and the restriction of $\gamma$ to $[0,\delta]$ has image in $K$, then, for $t\in[0,\delta]$,
$$w(t)\le\frac43 v_0,\qquad\bigl|\dot x(t)-\dot x(0)\bigr|_{\mathrm e}\le\frac49 v_0 .$$
Consequently, when $v_0>0$, the Euclidean coordinate displacement has component at least $\frac59 v_0\delta$ along the unit vector $\dot x(0)/v_0$. When $v_0=0$, the geodesic is constant and the displacement is zero, so no unit initial direction is selected.

**(b) Contained segments have small velocity.** Let $c_0:=\frac1{100}$.
Fix $r>0$ with $r\le\frac14$ and $\|\Gamma\|_K\,r\le c_0$. If the image of
the geodesic $\gamma:[0,1]\to U$ is contained in $K\cap x^{-1}(B_r)$, then
$$|\dot x(0)|_{\mathrm e}\le 4r .$$

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: strictly convex normal neighborhoods and the containment of small-velocity geodesics, section 2.2 printed pp. 26-27 and the convexity argument of Theorem 2.4
P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Proposition 2.2.6 with proof (printed pp. 12-13), the second-derivative estimate along geodesics in normal coordinates

items.title: Normal neighborhoods, convex normal sets, the position vector and the squared-displacement function
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), and let $\exp_q:\mathcal E_q\to M$
be the exponential maps of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. For an open set
$U\subseteq M$ write $T U\subseteq TM$ for the tangent vectors based at
points of $U$.

**(a) Normal neighborhood.** An open neighborhood $U$ of $p\in M$ is a
**normal neighborhood of $p$** when there is an open star-shaped subset
$W\subseteq\mathcal E_p$ of $T_pM$ such that $U=\exp_p(W)$ and
$\exp_p|_W:W\to U$ is a diffeomorphism onto $U$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
supplies such pairs). The **exponential coordinates at $p$** on such a $U$
are $u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U\to\mathbb R^4$ for a linear isomorphism
$\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$.

**(b) Convex normal and strictly convex normal sets.** An open set
$C\subseteq M$ is **convex normal** when it is a normal neighborhood of each
of its points; thus for every $q\in C$ there is an open star-shaped
$C_q\subseteq\mathcal E_q$ with $\exp_q(C_q)=C$ and
$\exp_q|_{C_q}$ a diffeomorphism onto $C$. It is **strictly convex normal**
when in addition any two points of its closure $\overline C$ are joined by a
unique geodesic whose image is contained in $C$ except for the endpoints.

**(c) Position vector.** Let $C$ be convex normal, let $p,q\in C$ and let
$x:[0,1]\to C$ be the unique geodesic with $x(0)=p$, $x(1)=q$ supplied by
the definition of strict convexity outside the endpoints; equivalently
$x(t)=\exp_p(t\,\exp_p^{-1}(q))$ for $t\in[0,1]$ and
$v:=\exp_p^{-1}(q)\in T_pM$. The vector
$$P(p,q):=\gamma_{p,v}'(1)=d(\exp_p)_{v}(v)\in T_qM$$
is the **position vector of $q$ with respect to $p$**; here
$\gamma_{p,v}$ is the maximal geodesic of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. By the Gauss lemma of
[[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]]
$g_q(P(p,q),P(p,q))=g_p(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q))$.

**(d) Squared-displacement function.** For a normal neighborhood $U$ of
$p$ the **squared-displacement function** is
$$D_p^2:U\to\mathbb R,\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p\bigl(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q)\bigr).$$
It is smooth on $U$ because $\exp_p^{-1}$ is smooth and $g_p$ is bilinear;
$D_p^2(p)=0$, $D_p^2(q)<0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is timelike,
$D_p^2(q)=0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is null or zero, and $D_p^2(q)>0$
exactly when $P(p,q)$ is spacelike. On a convex normal $C$ we write
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$, $D^2(p,q):=D_p^2(q)$, whenever the position
vector is defined.

**(e) Scope.** These are definitions inside the smooth Lorentzian model;
they assert no existence of convex normal sets (supplied separately by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]), no completeness and no physical
reading. The position vector is an element of $T_qM$, not a vector field and
not a coordinate displacement; $D^2$ is not a metric distance and takes
negative values on timelike-separated pairs.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: normal neighborhoods (Definition 2.2 printed p. 26), convex normal and strictly convex normal sets (Definition 2.3 printed p. 26), position vector (Definition 2.5 printed p. 27) and the function D^2 (equation (2.5) printed p. 27)
P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): normal neighbourhoods and exponential coordinates, sections 2.2-2.3

items.title: Existence of strictly convex normal neighborhoods: small coordinate balls are normal neighborhoods of each of their points
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Theorem 2.4 (strictly convex normal neighborhoods and the joint exponential diffeomorphism; coordinate balls can be chosen) printed p. 26, and Definition 2.3 printed p. 26
P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): normal coordinates and convexity, Sections 2.2-2.3 with Proposition 2.2.6 and Definition 2.2.7 (printed pp. 10-13)

items.title: The differential of the squared-displacement function and the position vector of the reversed geodesic
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), let $p\in M$ and let $U_p=\exp_p(W_p)$
be a normal neighborhood of $p$ with $W_p$ star-shaped, as in
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (a). Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$ for $q\in U_p$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$, and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))$.

**(a) Differential in the second argument.** $D_p^2$ is smooth on $U_p$ and,
for every $q\in U_p$ and every $w\in T_qM$,
$$d(D_p^2)_q(w)=2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

**(b) Reversal.** Let $q\in U_p$ and let $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$,
$\gamma(t)=\exp_p(t\,v(q))$, be the radial geodesic, so that
$\gamma(1)=q$. Then the reversed curve $t\mapsto\gamma(1-t)$ is the maximal
geodesic from $q$ with initial velocity $-P(p,q)$; consequently
$$\exp_q^{-1}(p)=-P(p,q)\quad\text{and}\quad P(q,p)=-\,v(q)=-(\exp_p)^{-1}(q)$$
whenever both sides are defined, and then $D^2(q,p)=D^2(p,q)$ by the Gauss
lemma of [[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]].

**(c) Differential on pairs in a convex normal set.** If $C$ is a convex
normal set ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and $p,q\in C$, then
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$ is smooth and for all $u\in T_pM$, $w\in T_qM$,
$$dD^2(p,q)(u,w)=2\,g_p\bigl(P(q,p),u\bigr)+2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Gauss' Lemma, equations (2.5)-(2.7) and the differential of D^2 (Theorem 2.6 printed p. 27)
E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: the position vector and its change under exchanging the arguments, section 2.2 printed pp. 26-27

items.title: Length monotonicity of the squared displacement: once a future causal curve in a normal neighborhood has a future timelike position vector, the displacement radius grows at least as fast as the accumulated Lorentzian length
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $p\in M$ and let
$U_p=\exp_p(W_p)$ be a normal neighborhood of $p$ as in
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (a). Let
$\sigma:[a,b]\to U_p$ be a future causal curve in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] (locally absolutely continuous,
with future causal nonzero velocity almost everywhere), and write
$$v(t):=\exp_p^{-1}\bigl(\sigma(t)\bigr),\qquad P(t):=d(\exp_p)_{v(t)}(v(t)),\qquad Q(t):=g_p(v(t),v(t))$$
for $t\in[a,b]$. Suppose there is $t^*\in[a,b]$ such that $v(t^*)$ is
future timelike. Then:

**(a) Propagation.** For every $t\in[t^*,b]$ with
$\sigma([t^*,t])\subseteq U_p$, the vector $v(t)$ is future timelike;
consequently $Q(t)<0$, and $R(t):=\sqrt{-Q(t)}>0$.

**(b) Length inequality.** For all $t^*\le t_1<t_2\le b$ with
$\sigma([t_1,t_2])\subseteq U_p$,
$$R(t_2)-R(t_1)\ \ge\ L_g\bigl(\sigma|_{[t_1,t_2]}\bigr),$$
the Lorentzian length of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]].
In particular $R$ is nondecreasing on $[t^*,b]$.

**(c) Derivative formula.** The map $t\mapsto Q(t)$ is absolutely
continuous and
$$\frac{d}{dt}Q(t)=2\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(P(t),\sigma'(t)\bigr)$$
at almost every $t\in[a,b]$.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: inequality (2.8) and the monotonicity of D^2_p along causal curves, proof of Theorem 2.9 printed pp. 29-30
E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: local maximization properties of geodesics, section 2.4 printed pp. 28-33

items.title: The initial cone step: a future causal curve starting at a point of a convex normal set has future causal position vectors near its start
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $C\subseteq M$ be a strictly
convex normal set ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]), let
$q\in C$ and let $\sigma:[0,T_0]\to C$ be a future causal curve in the
class of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] with $\sigma(0)=q$. Then
there is $\delta\in(0,T_0]$ such that, for every $s\in(0,\delta]$, the
position vector
$$\exp_q^{-1}\bigl(\sigma(s)\bigr)\in T_qM$$
is future causal. Moreover, if $\sigma$ is not constant on any interval
$[0,s]$, the position vectors for $s\in(0,\delta]$ are nonzero.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: the appended-timelike-geodesic argument in the proof of Theorem 2.9, printed pp. 29-30
P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): local cone structure and the timelike-geodesic smoothing argument, section 2.4

items.title: Local causality in a convex normal ball: causal reachability is the exponential cone, the Lorentzian length is bounded by the displacement radius, and null endpoints force the null geodesic
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $p\in M$ and let $C$ be a
strictly convex normal coordinate ball around $p$ as produced by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]], small enough that the exponential
chart
$$u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:C\to\mathbb R^4$$
of [[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
(for a $g_p$-orthonormal basis with $e_0$ future directed) satisfies
$$g(\nabla u^0,\nabla u^0)<0,\qquad g(\nabla u^0,N)>0\qquad\text{on }C;$$
such a choice exists because both inequalities hold at $p$ (where
$\nabla u^0=-\partial_0$) and are open conditions. Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$ and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))=\eta(u(q),u(q))$ on $C$, and let $J^+_C(p)$,
$I^+_C(p)$ be the sets of endpoints in $C$ of future causal, respectively
future timelike, curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with
image in $C$ starting at $p$. Then:

**(a) Causal containment.** For every future causal curve
$\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ with $\sigma(0)=p$ and every $t\in[0,1]$: the position
vector $v(\sigma(t))$ is future causal or zero; equivalently
$D_p^2(\sigma(t))\le0$ and $u^0(\sigma(t))\ge0$.

**(b) Cone characterizations.** With $\mathcal C^+$, $\mathcal T^+$,
$\mathcal N^+$ the sets of future causal or zero, future timelike, and
future null nonzero vectors of $\exp_p^{-1}(C)$ respectively,
$$J^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal C^+),\qquad I^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal T^+),\qquad J^+_C(p)\setminus\bigl(I^+_C(p)\cup\{p\}\bigr)=\exp_p(\mathcal N^+).$$

**(c) Null rigidity.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$, and let $\hat s\in(0,1]$ satisfy: $v(\sigma(\hat s))$ is
future null nonzero and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for every $t\in(0,\hat s]$. Then
there are $v_0\in\mathcal N^+$ and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous
surjection $\varphi:[0,\hat s]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for $0\le t\le\hat s$.

**(d) Length maximality.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$. Then
$$L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-D_p^2\bigl(\sigma(1)\bigr)}=\sqrt{-g_p\bigl(v(\sigma(1)),v(\sigma(1))\bigr)} .$$
If moreover $v(\sigma(1))$ is future timelike and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for all
$t\in(0,1]$, then equality holds if and only if there are $v_0$ future
timelike and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous surjection
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for all $t$.

references.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): normal coordinates, the function sigma_p and the local causality theorem, Proposition 2.2.3 printed pp. 8-12, Proposition 2.4.5 with Lemmas 2.4.8-2.4.9 and Corollary 2.4.10 printed pp. 20-24

E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Gauss' Lemma (Theorem 2.6 printed p. 27) and local maximization properties of geodesics (Theorem 2.9 and Corollary 2.10 printed pp. 29-32)

items.title: A causal curve in a convex normal ball whose position vector is null at one time has null velocity almost everywhere up to that time
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$ and let $C$ be a strictly convex normal ball around $p$ satisfying
the hypotheses of [[thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone]], with the
exponential chart $u$, the position vector $P(p,q)$ and
$D_p^2(q)=g_p(\exp_p^{-1}q,\exp_p^{-1}q)$. Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be a
future causal curve with $\sigma(0)=p$ and suppose that
$D_p^2(\sigma(t_0))=0$ for some $t_0\in(0,1]$. Then:

**(a)** $D_p^2(\sigma(t))=0$ for every $t\in[0,t_0]$, and
$u^0(\sigma(t))\ge0$;

**(b)** the velocity $\sigma'(t)$ is null (or does not exist) for almost
every $t\in[0,t_0]$, and consequently $L_g(\sigma|_{[0,t_0]})=0$.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: the equality analysis in the proof of Theorem 2.9, printed pp. 29-30
P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): the identity (2.4.13) and its equality case, Corollary 2.4.10 printed pp. 23-24

items.title: Lorentzian length as a refined sum of local separations, and upper semicontinuity of the length under uniform convergence
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $L_g$ be the Lorentzian
length functional of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]] on future
causal curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). For a strictly
convex normal ball $U$ ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and
$p,q\in U$ put
$$d_U(p,q):=\sqrt{\max\bigl(0,-g_p(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q))\bigr)},$$
a continuous function of $(p,q)$ on $U\times U$
([[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c)).

**(a) Refined sums.** Let $\alpha:[a,b]\to M$ be a future causal curve and
let $(\mathcal P_N)$ be a sequence of partitions
$a=t_0^N<t_1^N<\dots<t_{m_N}^N=b$ with mesh tending to zero such that every
subarc $\alpha([t_i^N,t_{i+1}^N])$ is contained in a strictly convex normal
ball $U_i^N$ (such partitions exist and may be obtained from any fixed finite
cover of $\alpha([a,b])$ by strictly convex normal balls and a Lebesgue-number
subdivision). Then
$$L_g(\alpha)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{i=0}^{m_N-1}d_{U_i^N}\bigl(\alpha(t_i^N),\alpha(t_{i+1}^N)\bigr).$$
In particular the limit is independent of the choice of the partitions and of
the balls $U_i^N$.

**(b) Upper semicontinuity.** Let $\alpha_k:[a,b]\to M$ be future causal
curves converging to $\alpha:[a,b]\to M$ uniformly on $[a,b]$ (in the manifold
topology, equivalently along any Riemannian distance). Then
$$\limsup_{k\to\infty}L_g(\alpha_k)\le L_g(\alpha).$$

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Theorems 2.37 and 2.41 on the Lorentzian distance and length upper semicontinuity, printed pp. 41-44
S. W. Hawking and G. F. R. Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time, Cambridge University Press (1973): the Lorentzian distance and its semicontinuity, section 4.1

items.title: Pointwise local causality: closed cones, openness of the local chronological future, no local closed causal curves, corner smoothing and closedness of the local causal relation
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$. For every $x\in M$ there is an open
neighborhood $B$ of $x$, a strictly convex normal ball satisfying the
hypotheses of [[thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone]] with base point
$x$, such that, writing $J_B(x)$, $I_B(x)\subseteq B$ for the endpoints in
$B$ of future causal, respectively future timelike, curves with image in
$B$ starting at $x$, and $\mathcal C^+,\mathcal T^+,\mathcal N^+$ for the
future causal or zero, future timelike, and future null nonzero vectors of
$\exp_x^{-1}(B)$:

**(a)** $J_B(x)=\exp_x(\mathcal C^+)$, $I_B(x)=\exp_x(\mathcal T^+)$, and
$J_B(x)\setminus(I_B(x)\cup\{x\})=\exp_x(\mathcal N^+)$;

**(b)** $J_B(x)$ and $J_B(x)\setminus I_B(x)$ are closed in $B$ and
$I_B(x)$ is open in $B$;

**(c)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to B$
with $\gamma(0)=\gamma(1)=x$;

**(d) corner smoothing.** if $\gamma:[0,1]\to B$ is future causal with
$\gamma(0)=x$ and there is $t_0$ at which $\gamma'(t_0)$ is future
timelike, then $\gamma(1)\in I_B(x)$;

**(e) closed relation at fixed base.** if $q_n\in J_B(x)$ and
$q_n\to q\in B$, then $q\in J_B(x)$. The same holds for $J_B(x)\setminus I_B(x)$, the future null boundary including the vertex $x$. A sequence in $I_B(x)$ may have a null or zero limit, and a sequence in $\exp_x(\mathcal N^+)$ may converge to $x$; in either case its limit remains in $J_B(x)$.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Theorem 2.9, Corollary 2.10 and Theorem 2.11 printed pp. 29-32
P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Proposition 2.4.5, Proposition 2.4.7 and Corollary 2.4.10, printed pp. 20-24

items.title: Equivalence of the absolutely-continuous and continuous causal conventions, and one-sided inextendible extensions
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).
Call a map $x:I\to M$ a **geodesically connectible continuous causal curve**
when it is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and for every strictly convex
normal ball $C$ as produced by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]
([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b)) and all
$t_1<t_2$ in $I$ with $x([t_1,t_2])\subseteq C$, the endpoints $x(t_1)$ and
$x(t_2)$ are joined by a future causal geodesic whose image is contained in
$C$. Write $\le$ for the causal relation of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] (defined by locally absolutely
continuous future causal curves) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat .$$

**(a) Absolutely continuous implies connectible.** Every future causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve.

**(b) Connectible curves give causal relations.** Let $x:I\to M$ be a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve and let $t_1<t_2$ in $I$.
Then for every open neighborhood $W$ of $x([t_1,t_2])$ there is a piecewise
smooth future causal curve $\eta:[t_1,t_2]\to W$ with $\eta(t_1)=x(t_1)$ and
$\eta(t_2)=x(t_2)$ (in particular a locally absolutely continuous future
causal curve, so $x(t_1)\le x(t_2)$ in the relation defined by
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

**(c) Equality of relations.** For $p,q\in M$ the following are equivalent:
$p\le q$; $p=q$ or there is a geodesically connectible continuous causal
curve with endpoints $p,q$.

**(d) One-sided extension.** Let $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ be a
future-inextendible future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d). Then there is an
inextendible future causal curve $\gamma^*:I^*\to M$ with
$[0,\infty)\subseteq I^*\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $\gamma^*|_{[0,\infty)}=\gamma$;
that is, $\gamma$ is contained in a curve that is both future- and
past-inextendible. The dual statement holds for past-inextendible curves.

No choice principle is used. The extension in (d) is not asserted to be
unique.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: continuous causal curves and Theorem 2.12 with Remark 2.14 (printed pp. 32-33), Definition 2.16 (printed p. 33) and Lemma 2.17 (printed pp. 33-34)
S. W. Hawking and G. F. R. Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time, Cambridge University Press (1973): causal curves, their local Lipschitz property and the causal relation, section 6.2

items.title: Openness of the chronological future and past, openness of the chronological relation, and closure of future and past sets
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, with the
relations $\ll$, $\le$ and the sets $I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] and the future and past sets of
[[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]]. Then:

**(a) Openness.** For every $x\in M$ the chronological future $I^+(x)$ and
the chronological past $I^-(x)$ are open subsets of $M$.

**(b) The chronological relation is open.** The set
$$\{(x,y)\in M\times M:\ x\ll y\}$$
is open in the product topology of $M\times M$.

**(c) Closure of future and past sets.** Let $F\subseteq M$ be a future set,
that is $I^+(F)\subseteq F$. Then every $q\in\overline F$ satisfies
$I^+(q)\subseteq F$. Dually, if $P$ is a past set ($I^-(P)\subseteq P$) and
$q\in\overline P$, then $I^-(q)\subseteq P$.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: the chronological relation and its openness (section 1.11 and Proposition 2.4 printed pp. 15-16 and p. 26), future and past sets (Definition 2.83 printed p. 59)
S. W. Hawking and G. F. R. Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time, Cambridge University Press (1973): openness of the chronological relation, section 6.1

items.title: Basic limit curve lemma: arclength-parametrized causal curves have causal limit curves on compact parameter intervals and future-inextendible limits on half-lines
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $h$ be a smooth positive
definite metric on $M$ such that $(M,d_h)$ is complete in each connected
component and every closed $d_h$-bounded subset is compact (both hold for the
metric $h'$ of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]).

**(a) Compact parameter intervals.** Let $T>0$ and let
$\alpha_k:[0,T]\to M$ be future causal curves
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) parametrized by $h$-arclength,
$\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$, with
$\alpha_k(0)\to p\in M$. Then some subsequence (still written $\alpha_k$)
converges uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,T]$ to a map
$\alpha:[0,T]\to M$ with:

**(a1)** $\alpha(0)=p$ and $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le|t-s|$ for all
$s,t\in[0,T]$;

**(a2)** $\alpha$ is a geodesically connectible continuous causal curve in
the sense of [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]];

**(a3)** $\alpha$ is a future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]; and for every chart $U$ of the
kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (b), with
domination constant $K$ and time coordinate $x^0$, there is a constant
$C\ge1$, depending only on the chart and $h$, such that
$$t-s\le C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(t))-x^0(\alpha(s))\bigr)$$
whenever $s<t$ and $\alpha([s,t])\subseteq U$;

**(a4)** $\alpha$ is not constant on any nondegenerate parameter interval.

**(b) Half-lines.** Let $\gamma_k:I_k\to M$ be future causal curves
parametrized by $h$-arclength whose intervals $I_k\ni0$ satisfy
$[0,n]\subseteq I_k$ for every $k$ once $n$ is fixed (for instance
$I_k=[0,b_k]$ with $b_k\to\infty$), and suppose $\gamma_k(0)\to p$. Then
some subsequence converges uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of
$[0,\infty)$ to a future causal curve $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ satisfying
(a1)-(a4) on compact subintervals and which is future-inextendible
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)). A dual statement
holds, in the time-reversed orientation, for curves whose intervals satisfy
$[-n,0]\subseteq I_k$ eventually; it produces a past-inextendible future
causal curve on $(-\infty,0]$ in the original orientation.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Limit curve theorems in Lorentzian geometry, arXiv:0712.3942v2: Lemma 2.7 and Theorem 3.1(1), printed pp. 6-8 and pp. 11-13
E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: limit curve theorems, section 2.11 printed pp. 45-49

items.title: Achronal boundaries are locally Lipschitz graphs, topological hypersurfaces and null for smooth volume densities
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$F\subseteq M$ be an open future set, so that $I^+(F)=F$
([[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]] clause (a)), and let $A:=\partial F$ be its
achronal boundary. Then:

**(a) Achronality.** $A$ is closed and achronal: no two distinct points of
$A$ are chronologically related in either direction. Consequently every
future or past timelike curve meets $A$ in at most one point.

**(b) Local Lipschitz graph.** For every $p\in A$ there are a chart
$(U,x)$ of the kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a)
and (d) around $p$, with $x(p)=0$ and constants $K$ and $c$, and numbers
$a,\rho>0$ with $W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$, such
that for every $z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$$L_z:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$$
meets $A\cap W$ in exactly one point, and there is a function
$\varphi:B_\rho(0)\to(-a,a)$ with
$$A\cap W=\bigl\{x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z):z\in B_\rho(0)\bigr\},\qquad |\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\quad (z,z'\in B_\rho(0)).$$
Thus $A$ is locally the graph of a Lipschitz function of the spatial
coordinates of the chart.

**(c) Topological hypersurface.** The maps $z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ of
(b), for all points $p\in A$, form a topological atlas on $A$: $A$ is a
topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology and its inclusion into $M$
is a topological embedding. No smoothness of $A$ is asserted.

**(d) Null measure.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mu$ be a measure on the Borel sets of $M$
which is locally absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure:
whenever $(V,y)$ is a chart and $E\subseteq V$ has $y(E)$ of four-dimensional
Lebesgue measure zero, then $\mu(E)=0$. Then $\mu(A\cap K)=0$ for every
compact $K\subseteq M$. In particular this holds for every smooth positive
volume density on $M$.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Theorem 2.87 (achronal boundaries are locally Lipschitz topological hypersurfaces) with proof, printed pp. 60-61, and Proposition 2.84 printed pp. 59-60
S. W. Hawking and G. F. R. Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time, Cambridge University Press (1973): achronal boundaries and Proposition 6.3.1, section 6.3

items.title: The push-up rule: p << q and q <= r imply p << r, together with the timelike-piece criterion
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ and the relations $\ll$, $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** if $p\ll q$ and $q\le r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(b)** if $p\le q$ and $q\ll r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(c)** if $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is a future causal curve and there are
$a\le s<t\le b$ such that $\gamma|_{[s,t]}$ is a future timelike curve, then
$\gamma(a)\ll\gamma(b)$;

**(d)** consequently
$$I^+\bigl(J^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega),\qquad I^-\bigl(J^-(\Omega)\bigr)=I^-(\Omega)$$
for every $\Omega\subseteq M$, and dually
$J^+\bigl(I^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega)$.

No choice principle is used.

references.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Lemma 2.4.14 (push-up lemma I+) and Corollary 2.4.19 with proof, printed pp. 26-28; Proposition 2.2.3 and Definition 2.2.7 (elementary regions) printed pp. 8-13

E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: the chronological relation as an open subset of M x M (section 4.2 printed pp. 111-118) and Theorem 2.11 printed p. 28

items.title: Cauchy sets are closed, split the manifold into past, set and future, and are locally Lipschitz graphs
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$
with $\delta(a)=\delta(b)$; in particular $S$ is achronal and acausal, and
the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of
$S$ chronologically precedes $x$;

**(b)** $S$ is closed in $M$;

**(c)** for every $p\in S$ there are a chart $(U,x)$ of the kind produced by
[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with
$x(p)=0$ and the supplier constants $K\ge1$ and $c=16$, and numbers $a,\rho,\eta>0$ with $\sqrt c\,\rho+\eta<a$ and
$W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$ such that for every
$z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$L_z=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$ meets $S\cap W$ in exactly one
point $x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$, and
$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $|\varphi(z)|\le\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. The cylinder $W$ may be chosen inside any prescribed neighborhood of $p$. Consequently the maps
$z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ form a topological atlas on the closed set
$S$, making $S$ a topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology whose
inclusion into $M$ is a topological embedding.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Cauchy sets and domains of dependence, Definitions 3.33-3.35 and the elementary properties of Cauchy sets printed pp. 93-97; Proposition 3.42 printed p. 96

S. W. Hawking and G. F. R. Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time, Cambridge University Press (1973): Proposition 6.5.1 and the elementary theory of Cauchy surfaces, section 6.5; achronal sets and their local structure, section 6.3

items.title: Two-endpoint limit curve theorem: bounded lengths give joining limits, unbounded lengths give two inextendible tails with the closure relation
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $h$ be the auxiliary
metric of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]], so that
$(M,d_h)$ is complete and closed $d_h$-bounded sets are compact. Let
$$\alpha_k:[0,b_k]\to M,\qquad 0<b_k<\infty,$$
be future causal curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]])
parametrized by $h$-arclength, $\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for
$0\le s\le t\le b_k$, with $\alpha_k(0)\to x\in M$ and
$\alpha_k(b_k)\to z\in M$. Passing to a subsequence, let
$b:=\lim_kb_k\in[0,\infty]$. Then:

**(i) Bounded case.** If $b<\infty$, there is a subsequence and a future causal
curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=x$, $\alpha(b)=z$ and
$d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le t-s$ for $s\le t$, such that the subsequence
converges to $\alpha$ uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,b]$. If $b=0$ then $x=z$ and
$\alpha$ is the constant curve at $x$.

**(ii) Unbounded case.** If $b=\infty$, there are a future-inextendible future
causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$ and a
past-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with
$\alpha^-(0)=z$, such that a subsequence converges to $\alpha^+$ uniformly on
every compact subinterval of $[0,\infty)$ and to $\alpha^-$ uniformly on every
compact subinterval of $(-\infty,0]$ (where $\alpha^-$ is the limit of the
curves $s\mapsto\alpha_k(b_k+s)$, $s\le0$, for large $k$). Moreover for all
$t_+\ge0$ and $t_-\le0$ there are parameters $u_k\le v_k$ with
$u_k\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $v_k\to\alpha^-(t_-)$; in particular
$(\alpha^+(t_+),\alpha^-(t_-))$ lies in the closure of the causal relation in
the strong sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (c):
there exist sequences $u_j\le v_j$ with $u_j\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and
$v_j\to\alpha^-(t_-)$.

**(iii) Coincident endpoints.** If $x=z$, then in case (i) with $b>0$ the
curve $\alpha$ is a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $x$
($\alpha(0)=\alpha(b)=x$), and in case (ii) the concatenation $\gamma$ of
$\alpha^-$ and $\alpha^+$ is an inextendible future causal curve
$\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=x$.

**(iv) Imprisonment.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be strongly causal
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (b)) and
suppose all images $\alpha_k([0,b_k])$ are contained in one compact set $K$.
Then $b\le L(K)<\infty$ where $L(K)$ is the length bound of
[[lem-gr-strong-causality-compact-length-bound]]; in particular the case
$b=\infty$ is excluded.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Limit curve theorems in Lorentzian geometry, arXiv:0712.3942v2: Theorem 3.1(2) with full proof, statements printed pp. 11-13 and proof pp. 14-17, and Lemmas 2.5-2.7 printed pp. 6-8
E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: limit curves, section 2.11 printed pp. 45-49; non-total imprisonment, Theorem 2.80 printed p. 58

items.title: The existence of a Cauchy set implies strong causality and compact causal diamonds
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

references.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Theorem 2.9.9 with full proof (a spacetime admitting an achronal hypersurface with nonempty domain of dependence is globally hyperbolic on that domain), printed pp. 46-50, and Theorem 2.11.1 (Geroch-Seifert) with the volume-function proof, printed pp. 57-60

E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Theorem 3.45 (interiors of domains of dependence are globally hyperbolic) with proof, printed pp. 98-99, and Theorem 4.119 printed pp. 146-147

items.title: In a globally hyperbolic manifold the causal relation is closed and truncated causal cones over compact sets are compact
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold that is globally hyperbolic in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(c): strongly causal and with compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ for all $p,q\in M$. Let $h$ be the auxiliary metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and let $\le$, $J^\pm$ be the
relations of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** the causal relation is closed: if $p_k\le q_k$ for all $k$ and
$p_k\to p$, $q_k\to q$, then $p\le q$; consequently $J^+(x)$ and $J^-(x)$
are closed for every $x$, and so are $J^+(K)$ and $J^-(K)$ for every compact
$K\subseteq M$;

**(b)** for all compact $K_1,K_2\subseteq M$ the set
$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.

references.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Theorem 2.12 on closedness of the causal relation and compactness of J+(K1) cap J-(K2) in globally hyperbolic space-times, section 2.8 printed pp. 42-44 (Theorem 2.8.5 and its corollaries)

E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Theorem 4.12 (closedness of the causal relation for causally simple space-times) printed p. 118 and Theorem 4.119 with the compactness statements printed pp. 146-147

items.title: Continuity and strict monotonicity of the chronological volume functions in a globally hyperbolic manifold
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a globally hyperbolic
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)) and let
$\mu$ be the finite volume measure of [[lem-gr-finite-smooth-volume-density]],
with $\mu(M)=1$, $\mu(O)>0$ for every nonempty open $O$ and $\mu(E)=0$ for
every chart-Lebesgue-null Borel set $E$. Then:

**(a)** for every sequence $p_k\to p$ in $M$, the indicator functions
$1_{I^-(p_k)}$ converge $\mu$-almost everywhere to $1_{I^-(p)}$, and
$$\mu\bigl(I^-(p_k)\bigr)\longrightarrow\mu\bigl(I^-(p)\bigr),$$
with the same statement for $I^+$;

**(b)** the maps $p\mapsto\mu(I^-(p))$ and $p\mapsto\mu(I^+(p))$ are
continuous on $M$;

**(c)** $J^-(p)=\overline{I^-(p)}$ and $\mu(J^-(p))=\mu(I^-(p))$ for every
$p$, and dually $J^+(p)=\overline{I^+(p)}$ and
$\mu(J^+(p))=\mu(I^+(p))$;

**(d)** if $p\ll q$ then
$$\mu\bigl(I^-(p)\bigr)<\mu\bigl(I^-(q)\bigr),\qquad \mu\bigl(I^+(p)\bigr)>\mu\bigl(I^+(q)\bigr).$$

references.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Lemma 2.11.2 (continuity of the volume functions V+-) with full proof, printed pp. 57-59

E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: the volume/time-function argument of Theorem 4.119 printed pp. 146-147, and Proposition 4.118 (global hyperbolicity implies causal simplicity) printed p. 147

items.title: Local Cauchy neighborhoods in a conically bounded product chart
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the locally absolutely continuous causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, and let $B_R\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be the open ball of radius $R>0$ centered at $0$, with Euclidean norm $|\cdot|$. Suppose $(s,\sigma):U\to I\times B_R$ is a diffeomorphism of an open set $U\subseteq M$, satisfying:

**(C1)** $\partial_s$ is future timelike and every $s$-level is spacelike;

**(C2)** there is $K\ge1$ such that $|d\sigma(v)|\le Kds(v)$ for every nonzero future causal vector $v$ based in $U$.

Write $S=s^{-1}(0)$, and compute the domains of dependence intrinsically in $U$:
$$D^+_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D^-_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\}.$$
Here inextendibility means absence of an endpoint limit in the specified open submanifold, and Cauchy intersection means exactly one parameter visit ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). Then:

**(a)** $D^+_U(S)\subseteq\{s\ge0\}$ and $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$.

**(b)** The corrected open collar
$$Q=\{q\in U:|\sigma(q)|+K|s(q)|<R\}$$
is a neighborhood of the entire slice $S$ in $U$ and is contained in $D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)$; more precisely $Q\cap\{s>0\}\subseteq D^+_U(S)$ and $Q\cap\{s<0\}\subseteq D^-_U(S)$.

**(c)** The open set $W=\operatorname{int}_U(D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S))$ contains $Q$, and $S$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(W,g|_W,N|_W)$. Consequently $W$ is globally hyperbolic by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(d) Generic spacelike and noncompact scope.** For every smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subseteq M$ without boundary there exist an open neighborhood $U_\Sigma$ of $\Sigma$, a smooth positive function $\delta:\Sigma\to(0,\infty)$, and a diffeomorphism
$$F:\Omega\to U_\Sigma,\qquad\Omega=\{(s,x)\in\mathbb R\times\Sigma:|s|<\delta(x)\},\qquad F(0,x)=x,$$
such that $s$ is temporal and $F_*\partial_s$ is future timelike. The intrinsic set $W_\Sigma=\operatorname{int}_{U_\Sigma}(D^+_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma)\cup D^-_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma))$ is an open neighborhood in which $\Sigma$ is Cauchy, hence is globally hyperbolic. Neither compactness nor global acausality of $\Sigma$ in $M$ is assumed. No positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is asserted.

references.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Theorem 2.9.9 with Lemma 2.9.11 (curves in the interior of the domain of dependence meet S, I+(S), I-(S)) and the openness argument of its proof, printed pp. 46-50; Proposition 2.2.3 and Definition 2.2.7 (elementary regions) printed pp. 8-13
E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Proposition 3.44 and Proposition 3.43 on domains of dependence and causal convexity, printed pp. 97-99

items.title: The Geroch volume function: a continuous strictly increasing time function whose levels are Cauchy sets
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the curve calculus and auxiliary-length suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a globally hyperbolic
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)) and let
$\mu$ be the volume measure of [[lem-gr-finite-smooth-volume-density]] with
$\mu(M)=1$, $\mu(O)>0$ for every nonempty open $O$ and $\mu(E)=0$ for every
chart-Lebesgue-null Borel set. Let $L:=\ln$ denote the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]]) and define the **volume time function**
$$t:M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad t(p):=L\bigl(\mu(I^-(p))\bigr)-L\bigl(\mu(I^+(p))\bigr) =\ln\frac{\mu(I^-(p))}{\mu(I^+(p))}.$$
Then:

**(a)** $t$ is well defined and continuous on $M$;

**(b)** $t$ is strictly increasing along causal relations: if $p\le q$
with $p\ne q$, then $t(p)<t(q)$; in particular $t$ is a time function in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(d);

**(c)** for every inextendible future-directed causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ one has
$$\lim_{s\to\sup I}t(\gamma(s))=+\infty,\qquad \lim_{s\to\inf I}t(\gamma(s))=-\infty;$$

**(d)** every level set $t^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)); in
particular it is acausal, and it is met in exactly one parameter value by
every inextendible causal curve.

No smoothness of $t$ is asserted.

references.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Theorem 2.11.1 with the volume-function proof (Lemma 2.11.2 on continuity, Lemma 2.11.3 on the limits along causal curves, and the passage to the ratio tau = V-/V+), printed pp. 57-60

R. Geroch, Domain of dependence, Journal of Mathematical Physics 11 (1970) 437-449: the volume function and its use in constructing time functions on globally hyperbolic space-times; E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019) 3, Theorem 4.119 printed pp. 146-147

items.title: Truncated causal cones J^+(K) cap J^-(S_b) over compact sets and Cauchy levels are compact
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let
$t$ be the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]] and for
$b\in\mathbb R$ let $S_b:=t^{-1}(b)$, a Cauchy set. Then for every compact
$K\subseteq M$ the set
$$J^+(K)\cap J^-(S_b)$$
is compact; moreover
$$J^-(S_b)=\{q\in M:t(q)\le b\},\qquad J^+(S_a)=\{q\in M:t(q)\ge a\}.$$

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3: Theorem 4.119 statements on causal compactness and the compactness of J+(K) cap J-(K) for compact K, printed pp. 146-147; Theorem 2.53 (limit curve theorem, case (ii)) printed pp. 48-49
P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): Proposition 2.8.1 and Theorem 2.11.1 (volume function levels and compactness arguments), printed pp. 42-44 and 57-60

items.title: Cone bumps: for every point of a Cauchy level there is a smooth bump with past timelike gradient on the truncated past cone
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the actual volume-time and causal suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a globally hyperbolic
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let $t$
be the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]] with Cauchy
levels $S_c=t^{-1}(c)$, and let $a<b$ be real numbers. Then for every $p\in
S_b$, every prescribed $\delta>0$, and every open neighborhood $O$ of $p$, there exist

- a point $p'\in M$ with $p'\ll p$ and
  $$J^+(p')\cap J^-(S_b)\subseteq C$$
  for some strictly convex normal neighborhood $C\subseteq O$ of $p$ with
  $\overline C$ compact, $\overline C\subseteq I^+(S_a)=\{t>a\}$ and
  $\operatorname{diam}_h(C)<\delta$, where $h$ denotes the auxiliary
  complete Riemannian metric of
  [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and
  $\operatorname{diam}_h$ its Riemannian diameter
  ([[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]]), and

- a smooth function $h_p:M\to[0,\infty)$ such that

**(a)** $h_p$ has compact support contained in $C$; in particular $h_p$ is
smooth with $h_p=0$ on $\{t\le a\}$, and $0\le h_p$;

**(b)** $h_p(p)=1$, and $\{h_p>1/2\}$ is a neighborhood of $p$;

**(c)** $\nabla h_p$ is past timelike at every point of $\{h_p>0\}\cap
J^-(S_b)$;

**(d)** the nonzero-gradient locus $\{q:\nabla h_p(q)\ne0\}$ meets $J^-(S_b)$ only inside
$\{h_p>0\}$; more precisely, $\{h_p>0\}\cap J^-(S_b)=
\{f>0\}\cap J^-(S_b)$ where $f:C\to[0,\infty)$ is the future-branch exponential cone function on $C$
constructed below, and on a neighborhood of every point of that set the
cutoff used below is identically one.

references.title: P. T. items.title: Weak steps: locally finite sums of cone bumps give a smooth step around each Cauchy level with past timelike gradient near the level
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the actual volume-time and causal suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a globally hyperbolic
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let $t$
be the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]] with Cauchy
levels $S_c=t^{-1}(c)$, and let $a<b<c$ be real numbers. Then there is a
smooth function $\tau:M\to[-1,1]$ such that

**(a)** $\tau=-1$ on $\{t\le a\}$;

**(b)** $\tau=+1$ on $\{t\ge c\}$;

**(c)** $\nabla\tau$ is past causal or zero at every point of $M$: with the
gradient of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] one has
$g(\nabla\tau,\nabla\tau)\le0$ and $d\tau(N)=g(\nabla\tau,N)\ge0$;

**(d)** $\nabla\tau$ is past timelike at every point of $S_b$ and hence, by
continuity, on an open neighborhood of $S_b$: $g(\nabla\tau,\nabla\tau)<0$
and $g(\nabla\tau,N)>0$ there.

The function $\tau$ is a **weak step** around the level $b$: it moves from
the value $-1$ below the inner level $a$ to the value $+1$ above the outer
level $c$, with a timelike gradient near $S_b$ and a causal-or-zero gradient
everywhere.

items.title: Strip functions: every inner strip carries a smooth function with past timelike gradient, constant below and above the outer levels
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the actual volume-time and causal suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a globally hyperbolic
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let $t$
be the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]], and let
$a<a'<c'<c$ be real numbers. Then there is a smooth function
$v:M\to[-1,1]$ such that

**(a)** $v=-1$ on $\{t\le a\}$ and $v=+1$ on $\{t\ge c\}$;

**(b)** $\nabla v$ is past causal or zero at every point of $M$;

**(c)** $\nabla v$ is past timelike at every point of the inner strip
$\{a'\le t\le c'\}$.

items.title: Smooth Cauchy temporal splitting: a global temporal function with Cauchy levels and an orthogonal complete flow
items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), and let
$t$ be the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]]. Then
there exist a smooth function $T:M\to\mathbb R$ and, with $\nabla T$ the
gradient of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], the
following hold.

**(a)** $T$ is a temporal function in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (e): smooth,
$g(\nabla T,\nabla T)<0$ and $g(\nabla T,N)>0$ everywhere.

**(b)** Every level set $S_c:=T^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is a Cauchy
hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clauses (a)
and (c)): it is a spacelike embedded hypersurface and every inextendible
causal curve meets it in exactly one parameter value. In particular $T$ is
surjective.

**(c)** Along every inextendible future-directed causal curve
$T\to+\infty$, and along every inextendible past-directed causal curve
$T\to-\infty$.

**(d)** The vector field $X:=\nabla T/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$ is smooth,
future-directed timelike, satisfies $X(T)=1$, and is complete
([[def-complete-vector-field]]): every maximal integral curve of $X$ is
defined on all of $\mathbb R$, so by
[[prop-a-vector-field-is-complete-if-and-only-if-its-flow-is-global]] its
flow $\Phi:\mathbb R\times M\to M$ is a global smooth flow
([[def-local-and-global-flow]]).

**(e)** The map $\Psi:\mathbb R\times S_0\to M$, $\Psi(s,z):=\Phi(s,z)$, is
a diffeomorphism and $T(\Psi(s,z))=s$ for all $(s,z)$; equivalently $M$ is
foliated by the Cauchy hypersurfaces $S_c$, each flow line meeting each level
exactly once.

**(f)** Put $\beta:=-1/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$, a smooth positive function, and
$h_T:=g+\beta\,dT\otimes dT$. Then $g=-\beta\,dT\otimes dT+h_T$;
$h_T(X,\cdot)=0$; and $h_T$ restricted to $\ker dT$ is a smooth Riemannian
metric, so the decomposition $T_pM=\mathbb RX_p\oplus\ker dT_p$ is
$g$-orthogonal with $g(X,X)=-\beta$. Consequently the pullback of $g$ by the
diffeomorphism $\Psi$ has no mixed terms,
$$\Psi^*g=-(\beta\circ\Psi)\,ds^2+h,\qquad h_{(s,z)}(v,w):=g_{\Phi(s,z)}\bigl((d\Phi_s)_zv,(d\Phi_s)_zw\bigr),$$
a sum of a negative definite one-dimensional form and the smooth family of
Riemannian metrics induced on the levels.

references.title: A. N. Bernal and M. items.title: Worked null corner: two non-parallel null legs compose to a timelike displacement and push up to strict chronology
items.statement:
In the flat model $(A,\eta,N)$ with global inertial chart $x=(t,y_1,y_2,y_3)$,
put $p:=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$, $q:=x^{-1}(1,1,0,0)$ and $r:=x^{-1}(2,0,0,0)$. The
straight paths $p\to q$ and $q\to r$ are null, so $p\le q\le r$, while the
total displacement $r-p=(2,0,0,0)$ is future timelike. This example verifies
the two conclusions of the push-up rule [[lem-gr-push-up-rule]] in this
explicit configuration: $p\ll r$, with an explicit future timelike curve from
$p$ to $r$; and it contrasts the non-parallel case with the parallel case, in
which the composition of two null legs stays null.

references.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019) 3: the push-up rule and the strict timelike conclusion from a null corner, section 1.11 printed pp. 15-16 and section 2.6

items.title: Worked flat-model cone bump: the exponential cone function and its past-timelike gradient in inertial coordinates
items.statement:
In the flat model $(A,\eta,N)$ of
[[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]] with global inertial
chart $x=(x^0,z)$, fix $\delta>0$ and the events
$p:=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$ and $p':=x^{-1}(-\delta,0,0,0)$. This example computes
the cone-bump construction of [[lem-gr-cone-bump-functions]] explicitly at
$p'$ and verifies, in the flat model, each clause of that construction: the
exponential cone function $Q$, the future-branch smoothed bump $f$, equal to $\varphi(Q)$ on $I^+(p')$ and zero outside it, its past
timelike gradient on $\{f>0\}$, and the normalized bump $h_p=\chi f/f(p)$
with compact support.

references.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011): light-cone smoothing by the function exp(-1/Q) of the squared displacement, printed p. 59

items.title: Worked flat slab: a rational temporal function with Cauchy levels, complete flow and orthogonal product
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat slab $(0,1)\times\mathbb R^3$ of
[[thm-gr-flat-slab-incomplete-geodesic-and-cauchy-slice]], with restricted
inertial chart $x=(t,z)$, restricted metric $g=\eta|_M$ and time orientation
$N=\partial_0|_M$, and with the Cauchy slice
$\Sigma_{1/2}=x^{-1}(\{1/2\}\times\mathbb R^3)$. Define the rational
function
$$T:M\to\mathbb R,\qquad T(x^{-1}(t,z)):=\frac{t}{1-t}-\frac1t .$$
This example verifies, by explicit computation, that $T$ satisfies all the
conclusions of [[thm-gr-smooth-cauchy-temporal-splitting]] in this model:
past-timelike gradient, Cauchy levels, complete gradient flow, and the
orthogonal product form.

references.title: A. N. Bernal and M. Sanchez, Smooth globally hyperbolic splittings and temporal functions, arXiv:gr-qc/0308090 (2003): the orthogonal splitting by a complete temporal gradient field, printed pp. 4-8

items.title: Counterexample: on the flat slab the coordinate time has Cauchy levels but an incomplete gradient flow
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "on every globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold, for every temporal function $T$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (e) the vector
field $X=\nabla T/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$ is complete, that is, every maximal
integral curve of $X$ is defined on all of $\mathbb R$
([[def-complete-vector-field]])."

references.title: A. N. Bernal and M. Sanchez, Smooth globally hyperbolic splittings and temporal functions, arXiv:gr-qc/0308090 (2003): completeness of the gradient flow is a property of the constructed temporal function, not of arbitrary time functions, printed pp. 4-8
